# Pagecairn v0.1.1

Pagecairn v0.1.1 completes the project rename across the application, source,
documentation, GitHub repository, and Docker Compose configuration.

## Install

This release is distributed as source and built locally with Docker:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn.git
cd pagecairn
git checkout v0.1.1
docker compose up -d --build
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` for local evaluation. Read the
[self-hosting guide](https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) before exposing a production
installation: port 3000 is plain HTTP and production deployments require TLS
through a reverse proxy with secure session cookies enabled.

## Updating from v0.1.0

The Compose project and volume key now use the Pagecairn name. A v0.1.0
installation's old volume is not attached automatically. Before updating, back
up the complete `/data` directory from the old checkout, then stop the old app
before switching versions:

```bash
docker compose stop app
git fetch --tags
git checkout v0.1.1
docker compose up -d --build
```

Restore the backup into the new Pagecairn volume and verify pages, attachments,
members, and revision history before removing the old volume or backup. Do not
run the old and new Compose projects together because both publish host port
3000 by default.

Follow the complete backup, restore, update, health-check, and recovery steps in
the [self-hosting guide](https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md). Never run
`docker compose down -v` unless you intend to delete installation data.

## Scope

This is a naming and release-consistency update. The focused product remains a
single self-hosted application container using SQLite, local uploads, and one
persistent volume. No external service is required.
